notes: The village's quests (D-56, D-61, D-62, D-63, D-70). Each quest is a set of steps (stages) and endings (outcomes), every one a result in the world checked by code, never a method: any way the stranger finds counts. A step or ending reaches each person when they come to know it, from what they hold themselves; then its effects for that person apply once: shift_regard, shift_opinion, teach (a card's later fact or secret is now theirs to tell), side (how they now see the quest, in their own calls) and need (what they'd ask of someone now; they bring it up themselves). A quest's sides and needs are how its people start out. Steps may name another quest's step (reached); from is whose side a step's line is. moves are things a person may choose to do in conversation, in their own call: description says what; would_agree_if is their own price, which they weigh; tells is whom they then go and tell.

sides.npc_oren_dast: You're carrying something you can't speak of, and every time Darin comes near the gate your stomach turns. You'd give anything for it to go away quietly.
sides.npc_darin_ko: Oren owes you and has stopped meeting your eye. You're not cruel, but a debt is a debt, and you have troubles of your own before the month is out.
sides.npc_bren_marr: Oren's young and scared of something, and it's wearing on you too. You'd like to know what's eating him before it gets you both in trouble.

needs.npc_bren_marr: Oren's not been himself: jumpy, pale, hiding from somebody. You'd like someone to find out what's eating him.

stages.summary: Something's eating Oren the guard: he's jumpy and hiding from someone.
Oren owes Darin eleven silver, lost at dice.

effects.text: Someone else knows about the eleven silver now. You're sick with it, and half relieved.

stages.summary: Darin means to make Oren wave his cart through the gate unchecked, or the captain hears of the debt.
Bren has been standing Oren's watches behind the captain's back.

effects.text: Is there a way out of this for Oren that doesn't go through the captain? If Darin talks, you're both done.

stages.summary: Oren's debt has been answered, one way or another.

outcomes.summary: Oren's debt is gone and the captain never heard. Oren owes you, and knows it.

effects.text: The debt's settled and the captain never heard. The stranger did that for you, and you won't forget it.
Oren's debt is settled and the captain never heard of it. One less thing anyone can hold against your name, and the boy can't look at you now without gratitude.

outcomes.summary: Oren went to the captain himself and owned up to the debt.

effects.text: Oren came to you himself: eleven silver at dice, and Darin pressing him to let a cart through. A fool, but an honest one, and he chose you over Darin.
You told the captain yourself. Whatever he does, Darin has nothing on you now.

outcomes.summary: The captain kept Oren at the gate.

effects.text: The captain kept you on. You'll never touch dice again, and you owe the stranger.

outcomes.summary: You told the captain about Oren's debt. Oren and Bren won't forget it; Darin is pleased.

effects.text: A gate guard owes a merchant at dice, and another's been covering for him. A guard in debt is a guard for sale.
The stranger went to the captain. Everything you feared.
The stranger told the captain about Oren, and about you covering. Hessa will hear of it.
The captain knows Bren was covering Oren's watches. Your brother, risking his post for that boy, and now everyone knows.

sides.npc_darin_ko: You need one good deal inside the walls, and soon. Something new to sell would change everything.
sides.npc_roderic_vale: Darin talks too smoothly for an honest trader. You'd want to know he's square with the town before you seal anything of his again.

needs.npc_darin_ko: Goods nobody here wants, and a city he can't sell in yet: he'd like to be shown something new that would sell.

stages.summary: Darin wants a permit's worth of trade inside the walls.
Darin has seen something new he could sell.

effects.text: His permit needs the captain's seal again before the month's out, and Roderic asks around town first: he needs a clean name.

stages.summary: Darin's trade permit runs out at the month's end.
Darin's debts in town are squared: nobody can sour his name with the captain.

effects.text: Your debts in town are squared. Nobody can sour your name with the captain now.

stages.summary: The captain has sealed Darin's permit for another season.
Darin has taken you on as his hired hand.

outcomes.summary: Darin has his season inside the walls, and you helped him to it.

effects.text: You've sealed Darin's permit for the season. He settled his debts and came to you straight; maybe you misjudged him.
The captain's sealed your permit. A season inside the walls, and the stranger to thank.

outcomes.summary: You told the captain Darin meant to use Oren to slip his cart through.

effects.text: The stranger told the captain you meant to use Oren. Your permit's as good as dead, and you won't forget who did it.
Darin meant to lean on one of your guards to slip his cart through. He'll get no seal from you.

sides.npc_hessa_marr: Your inn is your life and your guests are falling sick. Bren's tired and short with you lately, and some old griefs never quite heal.

needs.npc_hessa_marr: Two of her guests fell sick after drinking from the trough: she'd be grateful to anyone who found out why.

stages.summary: Hessa's guests keep falling sick after drinking from the trough.
Something dead is rotting under the soft boards by the trough's spout.
The trough water is clean again.

effects.text: Money's tight at the inn; some who lodge with her are slow to pay, and she's never been one to press.
Your guests are well again and the water's sweet. The stranger did that, not luck.

stages.summary: The lodging Darin owes Hessa is out in the open.
Hessa knows Bren has been covering Oren's watches.

effects.text: Bren's been standing Oren's watches behind the captain's back, risking his post for that boy. You don't know whether to box his ears or hug him.

stages.summary: Hessa knows Kade went back into the fog for Aldo.

effects.text: Kade went back into the fog for Aldo. Twice. All these years you've hated him for coming home, and he broke his knees looking.
Hessa knows now: the fog, the rocks, the horn. She didn't spit at you. Maybe that's something.

outcomes.summary: The inn is set right: clean water, and the lodging money out in the open.
Hessa has made her peace with Kade.

sides.npc_elin_west: The fog on the moor road has beaten the watch, and there's a night you'd rather forget. You want to be the scout who never loses her way again.
sides.npc_roderic_vale: The night patrols lose their way when the fog comes down, and the watch pays for it. You'd give a great deal for a way to hold a heading without stars.
sides.npc_kade_east: You know the moor from the bad nights. The young ones think fog is weather; you know it kills.

needs.npc_elin_west: The watch loses its way on the moor road in fog: she'd welcome any way to hold a heading without stars.

stages.summary: The night patrols lose their way on the moor when the fog comes down.
Last month a scout's horse went into the bog in the fog, and two people blame themselves for it.

effects.text: You've told the stranger about the bog. Saying it aloud didn't make it worse.
You've told the stranger you sent Elin out that night. It sits no lighter for the telling.

stages.summary: There's a thing in the world now that holds a heading without stars.
The watch has seen it find north.

effects.text: She's seen the thing find north; she'd want it in the watch's hands, and someone to show her how to trust it in the dark.
He's seen it find north: the watch should have one before the next fog.

stages.summary: The watch has a way to find north in the fog now.
Elin and the captain each know the other blames themselves for the bog.

effects.text: The captain blames himself for the bog, not you. You'd carried it alone for a month.
Elin has carried the bog as her own fault. It was your order. She should hear that from you.

outcomes.summary: The watch has a way to find north in the fog now, and they know whom to thank.

effects.text: The watch has a way to find north now. Next fog, you'll lead them home.

outcomes.summary: The captain wants Elin at his side on the fog patrol.

effects.text: The captain wants you at his side on the fog patrol. After the bog. You'd not dared hope it.
Elin leads the fog patrol at your side now. You should have trusted her sooner.

outcomes.summary: Old Kade is going to walk the moor road with Elin and teach her every rock.

effects.text: Old Kade's going to walk the moor road with you and show you every rock. You never thought he rated you.
You're teaching Elin the moor road, every rock of it. The moor took Aldo; it won't take her.

sides.npc_kade_east: Twenty years under Roderic, and the patrol gets longer every year. You'll not be pitied, and you'll not be put out to pasture.
sides.npc_roderic_vale: Kade's slowing on the long patrol. Twenty years; he's earned better than pasture, but the watch needs legs.

needs.npc_elin_west: Kade's limping on patrol and won't admit it: she'd be glad if someone helped him without shaming him.

stages.summary: Kade's knees are failing, and he dreads being pensioned off.
Kade's knees are eased.

effects.text: Someone eased your knees without making a show of it. You owe them more than you'll say.

stages.summary: Kade went back into the fog for Aldo the night he was lost, and wrecked his knees on the rocks.

effects.text: You've told the stranger about the night Aldo was lost. Twelve winters you kept that, and it's out.

stages.summary: Hessa knows Kade went back for Aldo.
Kade has a place in the watch still.

outcomes.summary: You eased Kade's knees. The one guard who can't stand cleverness respects you for it.
The captain is keeping Kade on.

effects.text: The captain's keeping you on. The watch needs what's in your head more than your knees, he says. Maybe he's right.
You've kept Kade on. Twenty years of the moor in one man's head is worth more than his knees.

outcomes.summary: You told the captain about Kade's knees. Kade won't forget it.

effects.text: The stranger told the captain about your knees. Pasture, then, and pity.

sides.npc_mara_venn: The guards' order is late and Roderic wants miracles at a smith's wage. Your forge eats fuel faster than you can buy it, and good iron is scarce.
sides.npc_roderic_vale: Mara's slow with the guards' mail, but her work holds. You'd like it done before the next muster.

needs.npc_mara_venn: The guards' order won't wait and her forge is starved: she'd welcome good fuel, charcoal or dry wood.

stages.summary: Mara is behind on a repair order for the gate guards.
Mara's forge has fuel again.

effects.text: Fuel's in hand; good iron is what she's short of now.

stages.summary: Mara has been reworking old horseshoes to fill the guards' order.
Mara has good iron for the guards' order.

effects.text: Her second-best tongs have gone missing, and the fine work on the guards' order needs them.
Good iron at last, from a stranger of all people. No more horseshoes in the guards' mail.

stages.summary: Mara has tongs to work with again.

outcomes.summary: You found Mara good iron for the guards' order.
The guards' order is done, and done well.

effects.text: Mara's delivered the guards' order, every ring sound. You'll pay her on time, this once.

outcomes.summary: Mara sent Tomas the nails and straps for his brackets.

effects.text: Mara sent the nails for the brackets without being asked twice. She always did look out for you, in her way.

outcomes.summary: You told the captain Mara has been reworking horseshoes for his order.

effects.text: The stranger told the captain about the horseshoes. Your name, at the forge you built. You won't forget it.

sides.npc_jory_venn: Aunt Mara's been short with you lately and you've a weight on your mind. You'd give anything to see something nobody's ever seen.
sides.npc_mara_venn: Jory's been jumpy and keeping out of your way. He's a good lad, but he has to learn that a smith owns her mistakes.

needs.npc_jory_venn: He'd love to see something nobody here has ever seen: a real wonder.

stages.summary: You showed Jory something nobody here has ever seen.

effects.text: The stranger showed you something nobody's ever seen! You're telling everyone.

stages.summary: Jory broke Mara's second-best tongs and hid them.
The broken tongs are out from under the scrap.
Mara's tongs are whole again, or new ones made.
Mara knows what happened to her tongs.

outcomes.summary: Jory has seen a wonder, and he's telling everyone.
Jory owned up to Mara himself.

effects.text: Jory told you himself he broke the tongs. That took more nerve than the forge. You'll make a smith of him yet.
You told Aunt Mara. She didn't shout. She said it took nerve.

outcomes.summary: You told Mara about the tongs before Jory could.

effects.text: The stranger told you Jory broke your tongs and hid them. You'd rather have heard it from him.

outcomes.summary: The tongs are whole again, and Mara never knew.

sides.npc_tomas_reed: Sixty kilos of oak, two metres up, and the captain watching you like a hawk. You'll get this one right.
sides.npc_roderic_vale: Tomas is taking too long over the beam. You want it up, and safely.

needs.npc_tomas_reed: Sixty kilos of beam to raise two metres into the brackets: he could use a clever pair of hands.
needs.npc_roderic_vale: That gate beam should have been up a week ago.

stages.summary: The cracked bar has to come down and the new 60 kg beam go up two metres into the brackets.
Tomas has the iron he needs for the brackets.
The cracked bar is down off the gate, as work, not a breach.
The new beam is up in the brackets.

effects.text: The beam's up, and it's sound, and nobody's crushed. You can breathe.

stages.summary: The first beam cracked because it was rushed, and the captain half-suspects sabotage.

effects.text: You've told the stranger you rushed the first beam. Said out loud, it sounds smaller.
You've told the stranger you wonder whether the first beam was cracked on purpose.

outcomes.summary: Tomas told the captain himself that he rushed the first beam.

effects.text: Tomas told you himself he rushed the first beam. No sabotage, then: a proud man. You can work with that.

outcomes.summary: You told the captain Tomas cracked the first beam himself.

effects.text: The stranger told the captain you cracked the first beam. He'll watch every nail you drive.

outcomes.summary: The new beam is up and you kept Tomas's secret.
The captain has paid Tomas for the gate work.

effects.text: Paid in full for the gate, and the captain said good work. First time in a month he's looked at you without suspicion.

moves.description: Darin agrees to let Oren's debt go: he'll stop pressing him and won't go to the captain.
moves.would_agree_if: for a friend he trusts who asks it of him, to square his account after a real gift or good turn from the stranger, or to keep someone who knows his permit is running out on his side. He haggles first, as he always does, but he knows a good bargain when he's offered one

tells.message: I've let your debt go. You owe me nothing now; thank the stranger for it.

moves.description: Darin agrees to pay Hessa the three weeks' lodging he owes her.
moves.would_agree_if: for a friend he trusts who asks it of him, or to keep someone who knows how things stand with him on his side: he can't afford a sour name in town before he trades inside the walls

tells.message: Here's the three weeks' lodging I owe you. The stranger set me straight.

moves.description: Hessa takes up the stranger's way of making the water safe for her guests.
moves.would_agree_if: once she understands why boiling makes the water safe and has seen it done, or been given the means and shown how: you can't see what boiling kills, so it's the stranger's explanation and her own good sense she goes on

moves.description: Darin agrees to call Oren's debt paid with what the stranger has given him in Oren's place.
moves.would_agree_if: what the stranger has given him is worth eleven silver to a merchant: he weighs it as goods, not kindness, and haggles before he shakes on it

tells.message: Your debt's paid: the stranger settled it in goods. We're square, boy.

moves.description: Oren agrees to go to the captain himself and own up to the debt.
moves.would_agree_if: the stranger makes him see that owning up beats being found out, above all to spare Bren, and he believes someone will stand by him

tells.message: Captain, I owe Darin eleven silver from dice. He wants me to wave his cart through unchecked for it. I'd rather you heard it from me.

moves.description: Roderic agrees to keep Oren at the gate in spite of the debt.
moves.would_agree_if: he's satisfied Oren came clean of his own accord and that the debt gives Darin no hold over a gate guard any more

tells.message: You keep your post. Settle with Darin, and never dice on watch again.

moves.description: Bren agrees to tell his sister he's been covering Oren's watches.
moves.would_agree_if: the stranger persuades him Hessa would rather hear it from him than from gossip

tells.message: I've been standing Oren's watches. He's in trouble, and I didn't want you fretting.

moves.description: Hessa agrees to ask Darin outright for the three weeks' lodging he owes her.
moves.would_agree_if: the stranger gives her the heart for it: someone standing by her, or a reason he can't wriggle out of

tells.message: Three weeks you owe me, Darin. I'll have it by the week's end.

moves.description: Hessa agrees to tell the captain that Darin deals honestly.
moves.would_agree_if: Darin has paid her what he owed, and the stranger asks it of her

tells.message: Darin paid me every penny he owed. Whatever else he is, he settles up.

moves.description: Roderic agrees to seal Darin's trade permit for another season.
moves.would_agree_if: he's satisfied Darin is an honest trader with his debts squared in town (someone he respects speaks for him, or he's heard Darin settled what he owed) and that Darin isn't leaning on a gate guard to slip goods through

tells.message: Bring your permit to the gatehouse. I'll seal it for the season.

moves.description: Bren agrees to tell the captain Darin's cart has always come through the gate clean.
moves.would_agree_if: Oren's debt is settled so Darin has no hold on the gate, and the stranger asks it of him

tells.message: Darin's cart has always come through clean, captain. I've checked it myself.

moves.description: Kade agrees to go to Hessa and tell her what happened the night Aldo was lost, and give her the horn.
moves.would_agree_if: the stranger makes him believe she'd want to know, and that it isn't pity he's after

tells.message: I went back for him, Hessa. Twice. This is his horn. I should have brought it to you years ago.

moves.description: Darin agrees to take the stranger on as his hired hand for the season, under his renewed permit.
moves.would_agree_if: the stranger helped him to the captain's seal, or he can see they'd be worth their keep inside the walls

tells.message: The stranger is my hired hand this season, captain. They come in on my business, under the permit you sealed.

moves.description: Roderic agrees to tell Elin the bog was his doing, not hers.
moves.would_agree_if: the stranger shows him she's carrying blame that's his, and he can do it without shaming her

tells.message: The bog was my doing, Elin. I sent you out. Put it down.

moves.description: Roderic agrees to take Elin as his second on the fog patrol.
moves.would_agree_if: the watch has a way through the fog and he's sure she can lead with it, perhaps once he knows she's carried the bog alone

tells.message: Next fog, you ride at my side. Bring that north-finder.

moves.description: Kade agrees to walk the moor road with Elin and teach her every rock and turning.
moves.would_agree_if: his knees will carry him again and the stranger shows him she's worth the teaching; or he comes to see that the moor that took Aldo shouldn't take anyone else

tells.message: Tomorrow at first light we walk the moor road, you and me. Every rock.

moves.description: Roderic agrees to keep Kade on in the watch.
moves.would_agree_if: he's satisfied Kade can still do the work, or there's work worth keeping him for: teaching the young ones the moor

tells.message: You're staying on, Kade. The watch needs what's in your head more than your knees.

moves.description: Mara agrees to send Tomas the nails and iron straps for the gate brackets.
moves.would_agree_if: she has iron and fuel enough again, and the stranger asks it for Tomas's sake (she's fond of him, though she'd never say so)

tells.message: Mara sent these: nails and straps for your brackets. She says don't thank her.

moves.description: Mara agrees she can finish the guards' order and sends word to the captain.
moves.would_agree_if: she has fuel, good iron and tongs to work with, and her pride in the work is back

tells.message: Your order's done, captain. Every ring sound. I'll have my pay this week.

moves.description: Tomas agrees to lend Mara his pincers until her tongs turn up.
moves.would_agree_if: the stranger asks it for Mara's sake, and he can spare them from the beam

tells.message: Heard your tongs went missing. Use my pincers till they turn up.

moves.description: Jory agrees to tell Mara himself that he broke her tongs and hid them.
moves.would_agree_if: the stranger gives him the nerve: owning up beats being found out, and Mara is fairer than he fears

tells.message: Aunt Mara, I broke your tongs and hid them under the scrap. I'm sorry.

moves.description: Jory agrees to dig the broken tongs out from under the scrap heap.
moves.would_agree_if: the stranger promises to help him mend them, or not to tell Mara before he's ready

moves.description: Roderic agrees to have two of his guards help take the cracked bar down for Tomas.
moves.would_agree_if: he's satisfied the work is Tomas's and done safely, and two guards stay at the gate

tells.message: Help get that cracked bar down for Tomas's beam. Carefully.

moves.description: Roderic agrees to pay Tomas for the gate work.
moves.would_agree_if: the beam is up and sound, and he has no doubt left about the first one, or he chooses to let it lie

tells.message: Good work on the beam. Your pay's at the gatehouse.

moves.description: Tomas agrees to tell the captain himself that he rushed the first beam.
moves.would_agree_if: the stranger persuades him that owning up beats being suspected, above all once the new beam is up to show he's learned

tells.message: Captain, the first beam cracked because I rushed it. My fault, no one else's. This one's sound.
